name: fuel_trims
description: Use when a petrol engine runs lean or rich, idles rough, uses too much fuel or stores P0171-P0175: trim pattern at idle and at 2500 rpm.
instructions: Call run_skill {"name":"fuel_trims"}: it samples STFT (0106), LTFT (0107), rpm and MAF for 5 s at idle, asks the driver to hold 2500 rpm in Park or Neutral (hold_2500_rpm), samples again for 5 s and classifies the pattern.
Read the pattern line and every part the digest says was not measured (a trim not answered, the rev hold not done or not reached): never judge a part the digest says was not judged.
With a lean or rich pattern, open fault_codes and use read_dtcs_detail on P0171 / P0174 (lean) or P0172 / P0175 (rich); open misfire when it is offered, since a lean mixture also misfires.
Check the coolant in the triage first: trims only mean something on a warm engine (80 °C or more, closed loop).
interpret: Total trim = STFT + LTFT. Within ±10 % is normal; +10 % or more is lean (the ECU adds fuel); -10 % or less is rich (the ECU removes fuel).
Lean at idle that improves by 5 % or more at 2500 rpm points to a vacuum leak: unmetered air matters most at idle (intake hoses, PCV, brake-servo hose, intake gasket).
Lean at idle and at 2500 rpm alike (improving by less than 5 %) points to the MAF sensor or fuel delivery (weak pump, clogged filter, injectors) rather than a vacuum leak.
Rich: leaking injectors, high fuel pressure, a sticking purge (EVAP) valve or a biased O2 or coolant sensor.
A cold engine runs open loop and its trims mean nothing: say the trims could not be judged rather than guessing.
On an LPG car running on gas, the trims also reflect the gas system calibration; compare with petrol when the driver can switch.

fiat-punto-2008-12: The 1.2 8v FIRE is speed-density (MAP sensor, no MAF 0110): a lean pattern with the vacuum-leak shape usually means an intake or brake-servo hose; there is no MAF to blame.
